'''Mark Kisin''' is a [[mathematician]] known for work in [[algebraic number theory]] and [[arithmetic geometry]]. In particular, he is known for his contributions to the study of [[P-adic Hodge theory#General classification of p-adic representations|p-adic representations]] and [[p-adic cohomology]].

Born in [[Vilnius]], Lithuania and raised from the age of five in [[Melbourne]], Australia,{{citation needed|date=December 2025}} he won a silver medal at the [[International Mathematical Olympiad]] in 1989<ref name="imo">{{cite web |url=https://www.imo-official.org/participant_r.aspx?id=1895 |title=Mark Kisin |publisher=[[International Mathematical Olympiad]] |access-date=7 September 2020}}</ref> and received his B.Sc. from [[Monash University]] in 1991.<ref name="Harvard Gazette"/> He received his Ph.D. from [[Princeton University]] in 1998 under the direction of [[Nick Katz]].<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=131465}}</ref> From 1998 to 2001 he was a Research Fellow at the [[University of Sydney]], after which he spent three years at the [[University of Münster]].{{citation needed|date=December 2025}}

After six years at the [[University of Chicago]], Kisin took the post in 2009 of professor of mathematics at [[Harvard University]].<ref name="Harvard Gazette">{{cite news |last1=Bradt |first1=Steve |title=Mark Kisin joins Harvard as professor of mathematics |url=https://news.harvard.edu/gazette/story/2009/05/mark-kisin-joins-harvard-as-professor-of-mathematics/ |access-date=20 December 2025 |publisher=The Harvard Gazette |date=7 May 2009}}</ref>

He was elected a [[Fellow of the Royal Society]] in 2008.<ref>{{cite web |title=Professor Mark Kisin FRS |url=https://royalsociety.org/people/mark-kisin-11756/ |publisher=The Royal Society |access-date=20 December 2025}}</ref> He gave an [[list of International Congresses of Mathematicians Plenary and Invited Speakers|invited talk at the International Congress of Mathematicians]] in 2010, on the topic of "Number Theory".<ref>{{cite web|title=ICM Plenary and Invited Speakers since 1897|url=http://www.mathunion.org/db/ICM/Speakers/SortedByCongress.php|publisher=[[International Congress of Mathematicians]]|access-date=15 August 2013|archive-date=8 November 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171108012153/http://www.mathunion.org/db/ICM/Speakers/SortedByCongress.php|url-status=dead}}</ref> In 2012 he became a fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>{{cite web |title=List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society |url=https://www.ams.org/cgi-bin/fellows/fellows.cgi |publisher=American Mathematical Society |access-date=20 December 2025}}</ref> He was elected to the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] in 2022.<ref>{{cite web |title=Professor Mark Kisin |url=https://www.amacad.org/person/mark-kisin |publisher=American Academy of Arts and Sciences |access-date=20 December 2025}}</ref>
